holidays.name: Global Beatles Day
holidays.description: Put on the Fab Four, sing along to "Hey Jude" at full volume, and debate whether Paul or John wrote the better tune. Fans all over the world celebrate the music of the Beatles today.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to June 25, 1967. On that date the Beatles performed "All You Need Is Love" during Our World, the first live international satellite television broadcast. It was watched by an audience estimated at around 400 million people.
holidays.funFact: The Our World broadcast had a crowd in the studio that included Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, Eric Clapton and Keith Moon, all singing along.

holidays.name: National Catfish Day
holidays.description: This is a day to honor the whiskered, bottom-dwelling fish that is a staple of Southern cooking. Fry up some cornmeal-crusted fillets, or just appreciate how strange and wonderful catfish are.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has been celebrated on the calendar for years by fans of Southern cuisine and fish lovers.
holidays.funFact: Catfish have taste buds all over their bodies, not only in their mouths. Some species have as many as 100,000, so they effectively taste the water by swimming in it.

holidays.name: Please Take My Children to Work Day
holidays.description: This day is a tongue-in-cheek counterpart to the well-meaning "Take Your Child to Work Day." It's for parents in the first weeks of summer break who are running low on snacks, patience and activity ideas. The idea is to hand the kids off to someone else's workplace for a day.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, humorous observance of unclear origin. It appeared as a playful twist on Take Your Child to Work Day, and it falls as school lets out for summer.
holidays.funFact: The original Take Your Daughter to Work Day launched in 1993 and was later expanded to include sons. This parody comes at a very different time of year, when parents are running out of summer-break ideas.
